cause: The first formal verifier invocation omitted the repository-required PYTHONPATH=backend environment prefix.
impact: The verifier exited before reading the formal line because the workbench package was not importable; no source or formal state was changed.

cause: The journal quality parser treated every level-one Markdown heading as Title, so conventional top-level headings such as # Abstract or # Methods were falsely reported as missing sections.
impact: Users or future report writers using one top-level Markdown heading per section could not produce an exportable journal report despite supplying all required sections.
lesson: Recognize explicit section names before applying the free-form-title fallback, and keep a regression test for top-level section headings.

cause: The new history-state regression test ran in isolation without initializing the fetchRunDetail mock, exposing an existing describe-order dependency in the frontend test fixture.

evidence.ref: npm test -- --run src/report/ReportView.test.tsx -t "generated reports persist to history"

impact: The isolated test failed before exercising the product behavior with TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'then'); no application source state was changed by the failure.
lesson: Initialize every async mock in the describe-local beforeEach so focused tests do not depend on execution order.

cause: The report save route accepted arbitrary unknown keys inside the nested revision source because the Pydantic field was a generic dictionary and storage validation checked only protected result-like keys.
impact: A report revision could carry unrecognized audit fields into durable storage even though it could not overwrite Run result fields.
lesson: Versioned nested report payloads need explicit allowed-key validation in the server store, not only protected-key rejection.

cause: The first journal quality implementation enforced a length floor but accepted an identical long sentence repeated enough times to satisfy that floor.
impact: A report could look long while remaining substantively thin, contrary to the user's request for a journal-style report standard.
lesson: Treat length as a floor only and add a conservative exact-repetition guard; do not attempt subjective semantic scoring in the deterministic validator.

cause: The first server-side revision validation rejected a new report record because its immutable source snapshot correctly pointed to the original parent report rather than the child record ID.
impact: Real Report-page prose edits would have failed at the save API even though the frontend allowed only narrative editing.
lesson: Revision IDs and immutable source IDs are distinct; bind a child revision to an existing parent snapshot instead of requiring identifier equality.

cause: The first parent-snapshot comparison treated omitted legacy optional fields as None on the child source while the persisted parent normalized them to empty lists.
impact: A revision from a legacy report without the newly introduced context/capability arrays would have been rejected despite an unchanged evidence snapshot.
lesson: Normalize optional snapshot metadata to the same empty-list defaults on both legacy parents and new revisions before comparing content.

cause: The new exact-repetition quality guard correctly rejected an existing LLM integration fixture whose long filler was one sentence repeated thirty-six times.
impact: The integration test no longer represented a substantively acceptable journal report after the validator was strengthened; production behavior remained fail-closed as intended.
lesson: Test fixtures must satisfy the same anti-boilerplate standard as generated reports; use varied evidence-specific prose rather than repeated filler.

cause: The real DeepSeek report request using the bounded 87-fact and 8-figure packet remained in Drafting beyond the browser acceptance wait without a preview or structured response.

evidence.ref: Report page remained Drafting after real DeepSeek generation attempt; run=20260803_181450_601295_bcce101a; packet=87/145 facts and 8/10 figures

impact: Real end-to-end acceptance did not pass; no report record or preview was created and no Run data was changed.
lesson: A valid evidence contract is insufficient if the default report packet cannot complete within a user-visible time budget; keep the full inventory in provenance while making the writer packet smaller and observable.

cause: The real DeepSeek V4 Flash report request with 46 selected facts and 4 selected figures reached the backend but the provider returned HTTP 503.

evidence.ref: Report page alert: LLM_UPSTREAM_ERROR: LLM provider returned an error: 503; run=20260803_181450_601295_bcce101a; packet=46/145 facts and 4/10 figures

impact: No report preview or durable report record was created; the Workbench correctly surfaced the upstream failure and did not fabricate a draft.
lesson: Real acceptance must distinguish packet/contract failures from provider availability and retry another configured model without weakening evidence validation.

cause: A real DeepSeek V4 Pro report request returned after one retry, but the journal quality validator reported missing model.estimation and diagnostics.robustness module coverage.

evidence.ref: Report run 20260803_181450_601295_bcce101a; packet 46 facts and 4 figures

impact: No report was saved and no preview was shown; this exposed an English capability-alias regression in the validator.
lesson: Capability coverage aliases must preserve English and Chinese terms without duplicate dictionary keys.

cause: The real report generation endpoint accepted a curated writer packet, but the save endpoint validated the generated text against the full figure inventory instead of the included figure subset.

evidence.ref: Real run 20260803_181450_601295_bcce101a: POST /llm/chat returned 200, then POST /ai-reports returned 422 while 9 of 10 figures were omitted from the writer packet.

impact: A valid real-model report could not be persisted, so no preview or history record was shown; the generated report was not fabricated or silently saved.
lesson: The authoritative save route must validate the same curated fact and figure boundary sent to the writer while persisting the complete provenance inventory and exclusion list.

cause: The real DeepSeek report response continued to emit rounded numeric tokens without immediate exact fact citations after the first corrective retry.

evidence.ref: Real run 20260803_181450_601295_bcce101a: the report contract rejected uncited numeric tokens 240 and 0.0335 after the first retry.

impact: The Workbench correctly failed closed without showing a fake preview; a numeric-conservative final retry was needed for real DeepSeek output to satisfy the journal evidence contract.
lesson: When a journal report still violates numeric citation rules after one correction, a final numeric-free rewrite preserves the evidence boundary better than accepting rounded values or injecting citations automatically.

cause: The report quality API was widened to accept structured or string violations, but one ReportView rendering path still assumed every violation was an object.

evidence.ref: frontend npm run typecheck: TS2339 at frontend/src/report/ReportView.tsx:1006, Property message does not exist on type string | ReportQualityViolation.

impact: The full gate could not claim type safety until the visible quality-warning path handled both API violation shapes.
lesson: When an API union changes for failure transparency, typecheck every rendering consumer and preserve both structured and plain-text diagnostics at the UI boundary.

cause: The full backend suite reported host sandbox-exec operation-not-permitted failures, while the golden suite reported artifact snapshot drift already present in the broad v1.8.6 worktree; the frontend suite completed successfully.

evidence.ref: bash scripts/gate.sh --full: backend 35 failed, 4584 passed; golden failures; frontend 184 files and 1596 tests passed before typecheck was corrected.

impact: A green full release gate cannot be claimed from this environment; the report evidence slice is instead supported by focused tests, typecheck, FMS verification, and a real browser/provider acceptance.
lesson: Separate product-slice evidence from host containment and unrelated golden snapshot evidence, and disclose the bounded full-gate gap instead of converting it into a false pass.

cause: The report evidence selection, failure transparency, journal quality validation, persistence boundary, and real provider preview flow passed their focused verification boundary.

evidence.ref: Backend report-focused 106 passed; frontend report-focused 41 passed; frontend typecheck passed; FMS verify --all passed; real DeepSeek V4 Flash preview saved with 61 verified cite chips and one artifact figure, and remained after reload.

impact: The scoped v1.8.6 report evidence slice has reproducible focused and browser acceptance evidence without claiming a green host-dependent full release gate.
lesson: Close the report slice only after the real model response, authoritative save, reload persistence, evidence subset/provenance boundary, citation rendering, focused tests, typecheck, and FMS process gate agree.

cause: The default sandboxed execution environment could not apply the native sandbox profile, so the containment and code-execution suite was rerun with the required host permission boundary.

evidence.ref: Elevated retry of tests/test_sandbox.py tests/test_code_execution.py tests/test_code_execute_routes.py: 33 passed.

impact: The native containment failure is classified as an execution-host limitation rather than a report-slice product regression; the unrelated golden snapshot drift remains open and is not rewritten here.
lesson: When a protected execution test fails at sandbox profile application, rerun the bounded suite at the required host permission level before assigning the failure to implementation.

lesson: Cross-view workspace panels need explicit async lifetime, zero-width dock behavior, persisted UI state, modal-aware stacking, and distinct load-error states before browser acceptance.

cause: Report review workspace implementation was verified with focused tests, the full frontend suite, typecheck, diff validation, report-focused backend tests, and persistent in-app browser acceptance.

cause: The corrected Report review controls passed focused tests, full frontend regression, typecheck, diff validation, and live in-app browser interaction checks.

impact: The requested Report review interaction corrections are accepted for this scope; existing dirty work remains uncommitted and no release action was taken.

cause: The left run-version picker aligned its selected button from a 6px top inset, while the right workspace tab strip vertically centered its selected item, leaving a reproducible 3px baseline difference.

lesson: For adjacent navigation strips, compare actual element rectangles instead of relying on visually similar container heights; encode the shared baseline as a regression contract.

impact: The left run-version separator and right Report review separator remain on the same row in both wide and narrow workbench layouts; additional versions remain reachable through horizontal scrolling instead of changing the row height.
lesson: A visual baseline fix must compare the separators that users see, not only the selected controls; wrapping behavior must be included in narrow-layout acceptance.

lesson: Verify the actual served stylesheet and the user-visible tab before claiming a layout fix; compare both separator rectangles and selected-control rectangles.

cause: The prior correction changed the left run-version picker to force a fixed single row. That violated the requested scope. The correct baseline is the untouched left picker: 6px top and bottom padding, 36px control, and 1px bottom border; only the right compact strip needed to match its 48px content-box row.

evidence.ref: After removing all scoped wb-run-version-picker rules and changing only the PanelHost strip, the user-visible tab measured the untouched left picker at y=90..139 and the right strip at y=90..139; separator delta=0. Both selected controls measured y=96..132. Frontend typecheck passed; frontend full: 187 files / 1623 tests passed; git diff --check passed.

impact: Only the right PanelHost compact tab strip changes; the left Versions CSS remains the existing global rule and its wrapping/padding behavior is covered by a regression assertion.
lesson: Honor the requested ownership boundary in UI fixes: adapt the target panel to the existing neighboring layout instead of normalizing both sides.

cause: The browser acceptance deliberately exercised the new node panel Float, Pin, and Collapse controls, but the resulting persisted floating state was left in the user's active Workbench tab. The screenshot showed the node panel overlaying the workspace in the expected floating/collapsed state, but that state was not an acceptable handoff state.

evidence.ref: Current Workbench tab was restored after docking the node panel: no node-panel-floating portal; PanelHost active-kind=node and data-collapsed=false; docked controls are Float node panel, Pin node panel, and Collapse node panel; left Versions row remains at y=90..139 and right panel tabs at y=90..139.

impact: The user's active tab was temporarily visually obstructed by test state. The state was reset before handoff; the feature still supports intentional Float, Pin, and Collapse interactions.
lesson: Browser acceptance must restore the user's active tab to its pre-test layout before reporting completion, especially when window state is persisted per project.

cause: The node panel header still rendered a standalone Close button beside Actions even though the workspace tab strip already owned node-tab closing. The first focused test run also exposed one stale fixture assertion using the wrong node tab label; both the UI and assertion were corrected before final verification.

evidence.ref: Focused Vitest: 4 files, 90 tests passed. Full Vitest: 188 files, 1629 tests passed. Typecheck and git diff --check passed. Browser acceptance verified docked and floating node panels: Actions precedes the shared Float/Pin/Collapse controls, no standalone Close exists, the tab strip retains Close Derived interaction tab, and the panel was restored to docked state.

impact: The initial focused test run failed on stale test expectations only; no runtime failure remained. The final UI has one clear node-tab close entry and consistent panel-window controls.
lesson: When moving a close affordance from panel chrome to a tab strip, test both the exact tab label and the absence of an exact standalone Close button; verify docked and floating portals separately.

cause: The floating node panel reused the complete right-side DetailDrawer tab strip, including the docked panel's negative top margin, so the detached window showed duplicated or clipped tabs and the detached node remained selected in the docked host. The first focused regression run reproduced the pre-fix failure; the implementation then separated the detached tab from the docked tab collection and gave the floating window its own tab geometry.

evidence.ref: Focused Vitest: 2 files, 65 tests passed. Full Vitest: 188 files, 1630 tests passed. Typecheck and git diff --check passed. Browser acceptance verified Float leaves Report review in the right host and moves only Derived interaction into the floating window without clipping; Dock returned the node tab to the right host and made it active. The browser was restored to the corrected floating state.

impact: Floating node tabs now follow browser-style detached-tab ownership: the right panel remains available for docked tabs, the floating window contains only the detached node tab, and docking restores that tab to the right-side strip.
lesson: Model floating panels as tab detachment rather than as a second copy of the host tab strip. Test tab ownership, active-tab fallback, clipping, and the complete Float-Dock round trip in both the host and floating portals.

cause: The node floating drawer retained the embedded DetailDrawer's 22px top padding and centered its 36px header toolbar, while Report review used a 12px header inset with top-aligned controls. Scroll surfaces also mixed native/default styling with the DetailDrawer's label-tertiary scrollbar treatment. A first-run style contract test reproduced both missing contracts before the implementation was changed.

evidence.ref: Focused Vitest: 3 files, 69 tests passed. Full Vitest: 188 files, 1632 tests passed. Typecheck and git diff --check passed. Browser acceptance measured the node floating toolbar and controls at y=151.703125 and Report review controls at y=152 (0.3px difference); both right-side scroll surfaces computed scrollbar-color rgba(196, 200, 206, 0.72) with thin width. The browser screenshot showed the node Actions and window controls on the Report review baseline. Left Versions styling was unchanged.

impact: Workbench primary reading surfaces and both floating panel families now use a consistent light-gray scrollbar. Floating node Actions, Float/Dock, Pin, and Collapse controls share the Report review top baseline without changing Float/Dock behavior or the left Versions presentation.
lesson: For cross-panel visual alignment, compare measured browser rectangles against the reference component and lock the intended CSS contract before tuning offsets. Keep scrollbar styling at the shared Workbench surface boundary so docked and portaled panels cannot drift apart.

cause: The floating node panel still used a wide text Actions button, the drag-node affordance was stretched by the shared button minimum height, and native CSS resize exposed only a bottom-right handle. A focused RED test reproduced the missing compact-control and four-corner contracts before implementation.

evidence.ref: Focused regression and full frontend Vitest passed: 188 files and 1634 tests. Typecheck and git diff --check passed. Browser acceptance measured 27x27px Node actions and Drag node panel controls, 16x16px hitboxes for top-left/top-right/bottom-left/bottom-right, and used real pointer drags on all four corners. Each corner changed width and height; top corners moved the top edge and left corners moved the left edge. The floating panel was restored to x=36, y=116, width=680, height=572. The integrated quick gate's backend stage reported 4584 passed, 35 failed, 5 skipped, and 1 xfailed; failures were sandbox-exec permission failures and existing golden snapshot drift, unrelated to these frontend paths.

impact: Floating node chrome now uses the same compact square control footprint as the shared window controls, with a visible compact Actions glyph and stronger drag-handle dots. Users can resize the floating node panel from any corner while preserving minimum dimensions and corner-specific anchoring. The repository-wide quick gate remains red only for pre-existing macOS sandbox-exec and golden-snapshot failures outside this UI change.
lesson: When replacing browser-native resize with controlled corner handles, test both hitbox presence and directional geometry with real pointer drags, then restore the persisted panel position and size before handoff. Keep repository-wide environment failures separate from feature-specific acceptance evidence.
